source.exercise: Thinking about the Text (A Baker from Goa)

questions.question: What are the elders in Goa nostalgic about?
answer_steps: They miss the good old Portuguese days.
They remember the Portuguese and their famous loaves of bread, and the traditional bakers.

source.exercise: Thinking about the Text (A Baker from Goa)

questions.question: Is bread-making still popular in Goa? How do you know?
answer_steps: Yes. The mixers, moulders and furnaces still exist and the fire has not been extinguished.
The thud and jingle of the baker's staff can still be heard, and sons carry on the family profession.

source.exercise: Thinking about the Text (A Baker from Goa)

questions.question: What is the baker called? When would the baker come every day? Why did the children run to meet him?
answer_steps: He was called the pader; he came twice a day, in the morning and again on his return.
The children ran to meet him for the bread-bangles he had for them.

source.exercise: Thinking about the Text (A Baker from Goa)

questions.question: Match the following: when were these bread items eaten? (marriage gifts; a party or feast; a daughter's engagement; Christmas)
answer_steps: Marriage gifts: the sweet bread bol; a party or feast: bread of all kinds.
Daughter's engagement: sandwiches; Christmas: cakes and bolinhas.

source.exercise: Thinking about the Text (A Baker from Goa)

questions.question: What did the bakers wear in Portuguese days and later? How did a baker live and collect his bills?
answer_steps: In Portuguese days a kabai, a single-piece frock to the knees; later a shirt and trousers between half and full length.
He collected his bills at the month's end from records in pencil on the wall; the business was profitable, as his plump body showed.

questions.question: Where is Coorg?
answer_steps: Coorg or Kodagu is the smallest district of Karnataka.
It lies midway between Mysore and the coastal town of Mangalore.

questions.question: What is the story about the Kodavus' descent?
answer_steps: One story says part of Alexander's army settled in Coorg after moving south along the coast.
Another theory points to Arab origin: the kuppia worn by Kodavu men resembles the kuffia of Arabs and Kurds.

questions.question: What are some of the things you now know about (i) the Coorg Regiment, (ii) General Cariappa, (iii) the Kodavus' right to firearms?
answer_steps: (i) It is one of the most decorated regiments of the Indian Army; (ii) General Cariappa, the first Chief of the Indian Army, was a Coorgi.
(iii) The Kodavus are the only people in India allowed to carry firearms without a licence.

questions.question: Name the river and the famous fish of Coorg, and three adventure sports you can enjoy there.
answer_steps: The river Kaveri; the mahaseer, a large freshwater fish.
River rafting, canoeing, rappelling, rock climbing and mountain biking.

questions.question: Look at these words: upright, downpour, undergrowth, sunrise. They are compound words. Explain 'a sea of tea bushes'.
answer_steps: 'A sea of tea bushes' is a metaphor.
It means the tea bushes stretched as far as the eye could see, like the vast sea.

source.exercise: Thinking about the Text (Tea from Assam)

questions.question: Mention the two legends about the discovery of tea.
answer_steps: Chinese: leaves from burning twigs fell into an emperor's boiling water and gave it a delicious flavour.
Indian: Bodhidharma cut off his eyelids to stay awake; ten tea plants grew from them.

questions.question: Where is the tea garden Pranjol's father manages, and what do Rajvir and Pranjol see there?
answer_steps: Dhekiabari Tea Estate in Assam.
They see a sea of tea bushes and women with bamboo baskets on their backs plucking newly sprouted leaves in the second-flush period.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*Our elders are often heard reminiscing nostalgically about those good old Portuguese days,*
*the Portuguese and their famous loaves of bread.*
*Those eaters of loaves might have vanished but the makers are still there.*

(i) Who are 'our elders'?

(ii) What are they nostalgic about?

(iii) Who are 'the makers'?

(iv) Find a word that means 'thinking of the past with longing'.

(v) Who are 'those eaters of loaves'?
answer_steps: (i) The older people of Goa.
(ii) The Portuguese days and their loaves of bread.
(iii) The bakers (paders).
(iv) Nostalgically (reminiscing).
(v) The Portuguese.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*Midway between Mysore and the coastal town of Mangalore sits a piece of heaven that must have drifted from the kingdom of god.*
*This land of rolling hills is inhabited by a proud race of martial men, beautiful women and wild creatures.*

(i) Which place is described?

(ii) Where is it situated?

(iii) Why is it called 'a piece of heaven'?

(iv) Who are the 'martial men'?

(v) Give a word from the extract meaning 'warlike'.
answer_steps: (i) Coorg (Kodagu).
(ii) Midway between Mysore and Mangalore.
(iii) Because of its great natural beauty.
(iv) The Kodavus.
(v) Martial.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*'Over eighty crore cups of tea are drunk every day throughout the world,' said Rajvir.*
*'Whew!' said Pranjol. 'Do you know, the first tea was drunk in China,' Rajvir added. 'As far back as 2700 B.C.!'*

(i) Who are Rajvir and Pranjol?

(ii) How many cups of tea are drunk every day?

(iii) Where was tea first drunk?

(iv) How long ago?

(v) What does 'Whew!' show about Pranjol?
answer_steps: (i) Classmates travelling to Assam.
(ii) Over eighty crore.
(iii) In China.
(iv) As far back as 2700 B.C.
(v) His surprise at the huge number.

questions.question: How does the writer show that Coorg is rich in wildlife?
answer_steps: Kingfishers dive for fish, squirrels and langurs drop fruit, and elephants enjoy being bathed in the Kaveri.
Malabar squirrels, langurs, slender loris and many birds, bees and butterflies are found there.

questions.question: How are Rajvir and Pranjol different in their attitude to tea gardens?
answer_steps: Rajvir is curious and excited; he has read about tea and its history.
Pranjol has grown up among tea gardens, so he is not impressed by them.

questions.question: How does the writer show that bread was an important part of Goan life and culture?
answer_steps: The pader visited twice a day and was welcomed by the whole family.
Marriage gifts needed the bol; feasts needed bread; Christmas needed cakes and bolinhas.
Daughters' engagements called for sandwiches.
Baking was profitable, and the furnaces and the trade continue even today.
So bread was linked to the daily routine and to every celebration.

questions.question: Write a short travel brochure entry for Coorg using details from the text.
answer_steps: Heading and location: between Mysore and Mangalore, Karnataka's smallest district.
Best time: September to March; coffee estates, rainforests, rolling hills.
Things to do: river rafting, canoeing, rock climbing, Brahmagiri hills, Nisargadhama, Bylakuppe.
People: the brave, hospitable Kodavus; the Coorg Regiment and General Cariappa.
